Article Title: Asian Para Games bronze leaves Suhas Yathiraj hungry for gold amid IAS duties and badminton
Article Text:
Suhas Yathiraj (Image credit: Instagram)

Third Paralympics, one big dream: Gold at LA 2028

Suhas Yathiraj (Image credit: Special arrangement)

IAS officer by day, shuttler by night

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Suhas Yathiraj (Image credit: Instagram)

Lee Chong Wei 's influence

NEW DELHI: Suhas Yathiraj was disappointed with his bronze medal at the Asian Para Games in Nagoya. Having beaten Indonesia's Fredy Setiawan in their group match just days earlier, the Indian shuttler had hoped to reach the final and fight for gold.Suhas lost the men's singles SL4 semifinal 23-21, 8-21, 15-21. He had chances to take the opening game but failed to convert them. After bouncing back to win the second game 21-8, he lost focus at a crucial stage of the decider.“Definitely not satisfied with bronze. I think if I had played up to my full potential, I would have definitely done better. In fact, I defeated Fredy of Indonesia in the group match in Nagoya only a few days ago,” Suhas told TimesofIndia.com from Aichi-Nagoya in Japan.“In the semifinal match, the first set was very close. I lost 23-21 and I had game point, set point, but I couldn't convert that. In the second set, I won very easily. In the third set, I think after 10-all, I sort of lost focus for two to three rallies. That is where he took the game. So, it was not my best day, I would assume. I would always love to win a gold medal. So, yes, I am a little sad from that angle,” he said.The defeat also reminded him of how important it is to perform under pressure at major tournaments.“It is the most important factor to win medals at major games because you might be training well, you might actually have the fitness and the skills. But if you don't recreate that during the major games, then probably it is of not much use in terms of professional success,” Suhas said.Suhas, an IAS officer, said he had never imagined representing India in international badminton a decade ago.In November 2016, he made his debut at the Asian Championships in Beijing and won gold. Since then, he has won several medals at major international events. These include bronze at the 2018 Asian Para Games in Jakarta, silver at the Tokyo 2020 Paralympics, another silver at the Paris 2024 Paralympics, gold at the Hangzhou Asian Para Games and bronze in Nagoya.The 43-year-old has represented India at two Paralympic Games, Tokyo in 2020 and Paris in 2024, winning silver on both occasions.With the Los Angeles 2028 Paralympics approaching, the big question is whether he can go one step further and win gold.The desire is there, but Suhas is not looking too far ahead. He wants to take things one step at a time.“If you had asked me 10 years ago, I didn't even know that I would play for India. But whenever I look at the medals and the love I have got from fans and sportspersons around the world, the journey has been quite satisfying. I have had the honour of wearing the Indian jersey and winning medals for my country,” he said.“I am grateful for what God has given me. I never imagined that I would become an IAS officer one day, an Arjuna awardee or a badminton player winning medals for India. I never imagined all this. But thanks to the Almighty for all these,” Suhas, who is also an Arjuna Award recipient, said.“So if God and destiny have been kind to me, I hope they will take me to a place that I deserve. I hope I can do the best that I can in whatever I choose to,” he added.For most people, the end of a hectic working day is a time to relax, spend time with family, play with their children or watch a movie.For Suhas, it is often time to pick up his badminton racket and head to the court. His day includes early-morning gym sessions, office work, inspections, meetings, video conferences and checking files. Despite his demanding responsibilities as an IAS officer, he makes time for badminton and follows a strict fitness routine to compete at the highest level.Balancing the two careers is not easy, but his love for the sport keeps him going.“If you choose what you love, then the journey becomes painless. You enjoy that journey. That's what I do,” Suhas said.Explaining how he manages his work and training, he said: “It is challenging. My training generally starts in the night and it always involves sacrifices. Probably others would be spending time with their family members or having leisure time. My leisure time is to play badminton. In badminton, you need an extremely high level of fitness. It's challenging, hectic but at the same time I love it.”“I don't remember eating sweets in the last many months. I can't recall when I had my last sweet. So, I almost don't eat sweets or fried food and am also quite conscious about the nutrition that I take,” he said.Suhas grew up watching Malaysian badminton great Lee Chong Wei and was inspired by his movement on the court.“Yes, I have always been inspired by so many top players in the able-bodied category. Growing up, I watched the matches of Lee Chong Wei and how he used to move around the court,” he said.“Even in India, the top shuttlers perform extremely well, whether it is Lakshya Sen, HS Prannoy or Kidambi Srikanth. I know them personally and have always admired how well they are able to compete at the top,” Suhas signed off.
Article Summary: Suhas Yathiraj was disappointed with his bronze medal at the Asian Para Games in Nagoya. The Indian shuttler lost the men's singles SL4 semifinal 23- 21, 8-21, 15-21. Suhas has represented India at two Paralympic Games, Tokyo in 2020 and Paris in 2024.

NEW DELHI: India signed off from the Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Para Games with their best-ever medal haul of 114 medals as the week-long continental competition concluded with a closing ceremony at the Mizuho Park Athletics Stadium in Nagoya, Japan, on Saturday.Double gold medallists Nishad Kumar and Mona Agarwal led the Indian contingent as flag-bearers at the ceremony, marking the end of a landmark campaign in which the country's para-athletes delivered historic victories, world-record performances and podium sweeps across disciplines.India finished fourth in the overall standings with 30 gold, 35 silver and 49 bronze medals, surpassing its previous best of 108 medals at the 2022 Hangzhou Games.Held in Japan for the first time, the fifth edition of the Asian Para Games brought together around 4,000 athletes and staff from 45 countries and regions. NEW DELHI: Indian para-swimmer Himanshu Nandal made his mark at the Asian Para Games 2026 in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, completing a hat-trick of bronze medals with another podium finish in the men's 100m freestyle S11 event on Friday.The 22-year-old clocked 1 minute 5.90 seconds to finish third, behind Japan's Uchu Tomita, who won gold in a Games-record time of 58.22 seconds, and China's Chuanzhen Sun, who took silver in 58.70 seconds.Nandal's latest medal added to his earlier bronze finishes in the men's 400m freestyle and 100m breaststroke S11 events. He became one of India's standout performers in para swimming, matching compatriot Ravi Budigina's three-medal haul at the Games, which comprised two silver medals and a bronze.Born blind due to optic nerve failure, Nandal grew up in a sports-oriented family in Rohtak, Haryana. He initially took up judo and went on to win medals at the national level before switching to swimming in 2021.The change opened a new chapter in his sporting journey, as he quickly progressed from domestic competitions to the international stage.Nandal achieved a significant milestone in 2024 when he became the first Indian blind swimmer to meet the Minimum Qualification Standard for the Paris Paralympics.A political science graduate from the University of Delhi's Atma Ram Sanatan Dharma College, he continued to build his experience against international opposition. In 2025, he reached two finals at the World Para Swimming Championships in Singapore.At the Asian Para Games, Nandal began his medal-winning run on Tuesday, clocking 5:10.91 to secure bronze in the men's 400m freestyle S11 event. He followed it up with another third-place finish in the 100m breaststroke before completing his hat-trick in the 100m freestyle on Friday.The S11 classification is for swimmers with visual impairment, including those with very low visual acuity or no light perception.Nandal's three-medal campaign in Japan marks another milestone in his progress as an Indian para-swimmer and adds to his growing experience at major international competitions.

She then teamed up with Nitesh Kumar in the mixed doubles SL3-SU5 final, but the Indian combination went down 21-11, 19-21, 14-21 to Indonesia's Leani Ratri Oktila and Hikmat Ramdani.Nitesh, the Paris Paralympic champion, enjoyed a successful day of his own, winning gold in the men's singles SL3 event before adding mixed doubles silver with Thulasimathi.The 31-year-old defeated compatriot and Tokyo Paralympic gold medallist Pramod Bhagat 21-18, 21-16 in the men's singles final."Last time I was close, I was leading 19-16 in the third set, and then I lost. So this time, winning it and again winning in two sets against Pramod is, of course, very special, and I think it's one of the rarest of the rare things to see," Nitesh said after his victory.Naveen Sivakumar added another gold for India, beating Indonesia's Fredy Setiawan 21-9, 21-17 in the men's singles SL4 final. Making his Asian Para Games debut, Naveen completed the win in 36 minutes.Pramod had to settle for silver after winning gold in the 2018 and 2022 editions. India's Nithya Sre Sumathy Sivan also claimed silver in the women's singles SH6 final after losing to China's Li Fengmei.India continued to collect medals across disciplines on Friday. Para shooter Mona Agarwal won her second gold of the Games in the women's 50m rifle 3 Positions SH1 final, setting a world record with 357.5 points. She finished 3.8 points ahead of China's Cuiping Zhang.In para archery, Harvinder Singh and Vijay Sundi won gold in the men's recurve doubles event. Sandeep claimed the men's 400m T64 title, while Haney won gold in the men's javelin throw F37/38 event.India also added silver medals through Nithya Sre Sumathy Sivan, Pooja Jatyan and Bhawna Choudhary in women's recurve doubles, Parmod Bijarnia in the men's 1500m T46 and Nimisha Suresh in the women's long jump T47. Jehan Madan and Shubham Wadhwa secured bronze in men's doubles para table tennis MD4.India's tally stood at 106 medals — 28 gold, 34 silver and 44 bronze — with the country fourth in the standings. The contingent is chasing its best-ever Asian Para Games haul of 108 medals, achieved at Hangzhou in 2023.
Article Summary: Thulasimathi Murugesan wins gold and two silver medals at Asian Para Games 2026. Paris Paralympic silver medallist defeats China's Yang Qiuxia and Xiao Zuxian 21-16, 21-13 in women's doubles final. Nitesh Kumar wins gold in men's singles SL3 event before adding mixed doubles silver. India's tally stands at 106 medals — 28 gold, 34 silver and 44 bronze — with country fourth in standings.

India's Mona Agarwal continued her golden run at the Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Para Games, rewriting the world record to clinch her second gold medal of the competition in the women's 50m rifle 3 Positions SH1 final on Friday. China's Cuiping Zhang finished second to take silver, trailing the Indian by 3.8 points.India's other finalist, Avani Lekhara , narrowly missed out on a podium finish, ending fourth. Avani had been among the leading contenders after the prone position but lost ground during the standing series, which proved decisive in the final standings.Mona had earlier teamed up with Avani for an Indian one-two finish in the women's 10m air rifle standing SH1 event on the opening day.She won gold with a score of 250 after the seventh series, setting an Asian Para Games record and surpassing Avani's previous mark of 249.6 from the 2023 Hangzhou edition.Mona's second gold came as India continued their push to surpass their previous best performance at the Asian Para Games. At the time of reporting, India had collected 103 medals: 27 gold, 33 silver and 43 bronze and stood fourth in the overall standings, with China leading the table with 354 medals.India's record haul at the 2023 Hangzhou Asian Para Games was 111 medals.

Article Title: Asian Para Games: Thulasimathi clinches silver in women's singles SU5, remains in contention for two more golds
Article Text:
Thulasimathi Murugesan

Thulasimathi falls short against Yang after impressive semi-final comeback

Two more gold medal opportunities await

Who is Thulasimathi Murugesan?

India's Thulasimathi Murugesan added another medal to her growing collection at the Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Para Games, settling for silver in the women's singles SU5 badminton event after losing to China's Yang Qiuxia in the final on Friday. The 24-year-old, who won silver at the Paris 2024 Paralympics, went down 18-21, 11-21 against the Chinese shuttler at the Ichinomiya City Municipal Gymnasium.However, Thulasimathi's campaign is far from over, with the Indian still in contention for two more gold medals in the mixed doubles and women's doubles events. She will look to make amends in the remaining finals as India aim to add to their medal tally.Thulasimathi, currently ranked World No. 2, could not overcome Yang in the title clash, with the Chinese player securing the gold medal in straight games. The Indian had produced a fighting performance in the semi-finals, rallying from a game down to defeat compatriot and World No. 1 Manisha Ramdass 19-21, 21-15, 21-13 and book her place in the final.The silver medal adds to Thulasimathi's impressive record in para-badminton, following her breakthrough performance at the Paris 2024 Paralympics, where she finished runner-up in the women's singles SU5 category.Thulasimathi will have two more chances to finish her campaign on a high.She has partnered Nitesh Kumar to reach the mixed doubles SL3-SU5 final, where the Indian duo will face Indonesia's Leani Ratri Oktila and Hikmat Ramdani.The Indians booked their place in the final after overcoming China's Li Mingpan and Xiao Zuxian in a hard-fought 42-minute semi-final. Nitesh and Thulasimathi prevailed 21-19, 14-21, 21-17 to secure their place in the gold medal match.Later, Thulasimathi will team up with Manasi Girishchandra Joshi in the women's doubles SL3-SU5 final. The Indian pair will face China's Yang Qiuxia and Xiao Zuxian, giving Thulasimathi another opportunity to challenge for gold against the Chinese shuttler who defeated her in the singles final.Born on April 11, 2002, in Kancheepuram, Tamil Nadu, Thulasimathi has established herself as one of India's leading para-badminton players. Her silver medal at the Paris 2024 Paralympics marked a major milestone in her career, while her performances at the Asian Para Games have further strengthened her standing on the international stage.She trains in Hyderabad under coaches Pullela Gopichand and Irfan Sait while pursuing a degree in veterinary science at Namakkal. In recognition of her achievements in para-badminton, including her Paralympic success, she was also honoured with the Arjuna Award.
Article Summary: Thulasimathi Murugesan won silver in the women's singles SU5 event. The 24-year- old lost to China's Yang Qiuxia 18-21, 11-21 in the final. She is still in contention for two more gold medals in the mixed doubles and women's doubles events.

Article Title: Erling Haaland, Jude Bellingham among stars who reportedly visit hospitalised Bayern midfielder Jamal Musiala following two on-pitch collapses in August
Article Text:
Haaland, Bellingham, Ekitike and Olise reportedly visit hospitalised Jamal Musiala, offering support as the Bayern star battles ongoing neurological health concerns/ Image: X

Haaland, Bellingham, Ekitike and Olise visit Musiala in hospital

Two collapses in four days: what happened to Musiala?

Bild

Bayern contract debate draws FIFPRO response

Süddeutsche Zeitung

From Chelsea academy prospect to Bayern's 71-goal midfielder

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Bayern's Jamal Musiala celebrates after scoring his side's sixth goal during the Champions League round of 16 soccer match between Atalanta and FC Bayern Munich in Bergamo, Italy, Tuesday, March 10, 2026. (AP Photo/Luca Bruno)

Jamal Musiala’s latest health setback has left the Bayern Munich midfielder awaiting further medical assessments after a neurological condition caused two on-pitch collapses in the space of four days and a reported relapse during training this month. As questions grow over his recovery and future at Bayern, Erling Haaland , Jude Bellingham, Hugo Ekitike and Michael Olise have reportedly visited him in hospital, offering support away from the public debate surrounding his performances and contract.Erling Haaland, Jude Bellingham, Hugo Ekitike and Michael Olise have reportedly visited Jamal Musiala in a German hospital, where the Bayern Munich midfielder is awaiting the results of medical tests.The reported gesture brought together four high-profile players from across European football, with Haaland representing Manchester City, Bellingham Real Madrid, Ekitike Liverpool, and Olise Bayern Munich. Having all spent time playing in Germany across different spells, whether as former Bundesliga rivals or current teammates, the quartet came together in a show of support for Musiala. According to GOAL, their visit gave him a considerable morale boost as he continues to deal with a neurological condition that has interrupted his playing career.The 23-year-old has temporarily stepped away from football after experiencing another setback. Spanish radio station Cadena SER, citing a source close to the Germany international, reported that Musiala has been feeling considerable pressure from the public discussion surrounding his form, salary and future at Bayern.The same source said the midfielder wants to concentrate on his treatment and recovery rather than become involved in arguments over his performances or contract. His hospitalisation comes after two collapses during Bayern's pre-season friendlies in August and a further relapse during a training session in November.Musiala's condition became a major concern during Bayern's pre-season programme in August, when he collapsed twice within four days.The first incident occurred on August 15, during Bayern's 3-1 friendly victory over RB Leipzig. Musiala suddenly appeared unsteady before falling to the pitch, prompting teammate Ismael Saibari to rush over and help him as Bayern's medical staff entered the field.The midfielder appeared dazed but was able to walk off. He recovered sufficiently to return to training shortly afterwards, and the episode initially appeared to have been a temporary setback.Three days later, on August 18, Musiala collapsed again during Bayern's 4-2 friendly win over 1. FC Heidenheim. He had entered the match as a second-half substitute in the 61st minute, but went down around eight minutes later.Players from both teams immediately formed a protective circle around him to shield him from cameras while medical staff treated him on the pitch. Musiala was visibly dazed as he was helped off and replaced.Following the second incident, Musiala addressed his condition in a statement on Instagram, revealing that he had been diagnosed with a neurological dysfunction causing brief absence seizures.He described them as “brief, temporary, but treatable absence seizures resulting from a neurological dysfunction”.Bayern board member for sport Max Eberl subsequently confirmed that the two episodes had occurred after doctors adjusted Musiala's medication for his pre-existing condition. The medication change was therefore identified as a factor in the August incidents, rather than the diagnosis itself being new.There was further concern in November when reports from German media said Musiala had suffered another seizure during a training session. The reported relapse led to further adjustments to his medication and hospital evaluations.German newspaperhas also reported that a change in medication triggered episodes similar to those experienced previously, with the recurrence affecting his performances. Musiala is now awaiting the latest medical assessments, with no confirmed timetable for his return to football.Musiala's health problems have unfolded alongside a contentious discussion about his position at Bayern Munich.Club honorary president Uli Hoeness has publicly questioned whether the midfielder's current performances justify his reported annual salary of €25 million. Former Bayern chief executive Karl-Heinz Rummenigge has also made comments interpreted as suggesting Musiala could leave the club.The remarks prompted criticism in Germany, particularly because they came while the player was dealing with recurring medical problems. Cadena SER's source close to Musiala said the discussion surrounding his future and contract had added to the pressure he was already experiencing.There have also been reports about a possible change to his agreement.has claimed that a verbal understanding exists to amend the contract in Bayern's favour if Musiala's recovery does not progress as expected. Reports from England have suggested Hoeness is fully aware of the midfielder's medical condition.FIFPRO, the international federation representing professional footballers, responded to the public debate by calling for any contractual concerns to be handled privately with Musiala and his representatives.In a statement, the organisation said:“Turning Musiala's health and future into a public debate only adds to the pressure on him. Any concerns about his contract should be addressed privately with him and his representatives. Contracts are there to be respected.”FIFPRO also rejected the suggestion that a player's injury or decline in form should provide grounds for a club to revisit an existing agreement.It added that “injury or a dip in form does not give a club justification to revisit previously agreed terms, just as a run of outstanding performances does not automatically entitle a player to a pay rise.”The intervention brought further attention to the disagreement over how Bayern's hierarchy has discussed Musiala's situation publicly, while the player remains focused on his health.Musiala joined Bayern Munich from Chelsea's academy in July 2019, aged 16, after spending most of his youth career in England. Born in Stuttgart on February 26, 2003, he moved to England with his family when he was seven, spending a year at Southampton before joining Chelsea in 2011.He spent eight years in Chelsea's academy before choosing to return to Germany and join Bayern's youth set-up. His progress through the club's under-17 and under-19 teams was rapid, and he made his senior Bundesliga debut in June 2020, aged 17.Musiala has since become one of Bayern's most important attacking players, recording 71 goals in 236 first-team appearances across all competitions, alongside two goals in 10 appearances for Bayern Munich II. He has also scored 10 goals in 46 senior appearances for Germany.His honours with Bayern include six Bundesliga titles, two DFB-Pokal trophies and five German Super Cups. He was also part of the side that won the Champions League, UEFA Super Cup and FIFA Club World Cup during the club's 2019-20 treble and subsequent sextuple-winning period. His tally stands at 16 major trophies with the club.Internationally, Musiala shared the Golden Boot at Euro 2024 after scoring three goals in the tournament. His development into a central figure for Bayern and Germany has made the uncertainty surrounding his health particularly concerning for both sides.For now, the focus is on the results of his medical assessments and whether the latest treatment adjustments can prevent further episodes. The reported visit from Haaland, Bellingham, Ekitike and Olise has offered him support from fellow professionals, but his return to the pitch will depend on his recovery.
Article Summary: Erling Haaland, Jude Bellingham, Hugo Ekitike and Michael Olise reportedly visit hospitalised Jamal Musiala, offering support. The Bayern Munich midfielder is awaiting the results of medical tests. His hospitalisation comes after two collapses during Bayern's pre-season friendlies in August and a further relapse during a training session in November. The 23-year-old has temporarily stepped away from football after experiencing another setback.

Article Title: Heartwarming gesture in MLS: FC Cincinnati to pay stadium tribute to famous hippo after freak accident with woollen hat ended her life
Article Text:
FC Cincinnati will honour beloved hippo Fiona with a special stadium tribute following her tragic death at the Cincinnati Zoo.

A tribute to one of Cincinnati’s most recognisable residents

How Fiona became a symbol of the city

The circumstances surrounding Fiona’s death

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Cincinnati face a difficult test against Nashville

Fiona became one of Cincinnati’s most recognisable residents after surviving a premature birth that left her weighing barely half the previous lowest recorded birth weight for her species. Nine years later, the hippo’s death has prompted tributes across the city, with FC Cincinnati preparing a special stadium display in her memory before their MLS Cup Playoffs meeting with Nashville SC.FC Cincinnati will honour Fiona, the much-loved hippopotamus who died at the Cincinnati Zoo last week, with a special tifo display before Saturday’s MLS Cup Playoffs match against Nashville SC.The banner, created by independent supporters’ group The Forge Cincy, will be unveiled in The Bailey, the club’s main supporters’ section at TQL Stadium, ahead of the 6.30pm ET kick-off on November 28.Fiona died on November 19, aged nine, after swallowing a woollen hat that had accidentally entered her enclosure. Her premature birth at the Cincinnati Zoo in 2017 had made her an international social media sensation, while her survival and development turned her into a symbol of the city.FC Cincinnati described her as a “beloved hippo who became a symbol of Cincinnati and captured hearts around the world”.The club will also make a donation to the Cincinnati Zoo and Botanical Garden in Fiona’s memory for every supporter attending Saturday’s match.The Forge Cincy began painting the tribute on Sunday in a garage beside TQL Stadium. The group has previously produced large-scale displays for important fixtures, including a two-week project for October’s “Hell is Real” derby against Ohio rivals Columbus Crew.Fiona’s story began with an unusually difficult birth. When she arrived prematurely in January 2017, she weighed just 13kg (29lb), approximately half the previous lowest recorded birth weight for a hippopotamus.Her survival required intensive care from the zoo’s staff, and the attention surrounding her recovery soon extended well beyond Cincinnati. She became a social media favourite, inspired an ice cream flavour and was even turned into a character in the city’s ballet.Her death prompted tributes from across the sporting community. Cincinnati defender Nick Hagglund, a local who is in his eighth season with the club, dedicated his goal celebration to Fiona after scoring in the team’s 3-1 victory over Orlando on the day she died.Hagglund shouted “that's for Fiona” while mimicking the ears on top of the hippo’s head. He later wrote on Instagram:“This one was for her @fionahippo @cincinnatizoo.“Cincinnati needed a win on the day after the passing of our beloved hippo, a symbol of hope and resilience for our city, and the lads answered the call.”Cincinnati Bengals wide receiver Tee Higgins also paid tribute, wearing a Fiona sweater before his team’s defeat by the Washington Commanders on Monday. Meanwhile, handlers of the blue hippo balloon at New York’s annual Macy’s Thanksgiving Parade will wear a purple patch in her honour.Fiona swallowed the woollen hat approximately 10 days before she died. According to the zoo, the item entered her enclosure accidentally after a visitor tossed it into the air. It caught on a ceiling fan, which propelled it through a small opening.Zoo spokesperson Michelle Curley said removing the hat had been impossible, describing the sequence of events as exceptionally unlikely.“We probably couldn't make [it] happen again if we tried,” Curley said.The zoo had previously explained that the hat could not be safely retrieved from Fiona. Hippos typically live for up to 50 years in human care, making her death at nine particularly premature.The tribute will take place before the second match of FC Cincinnati’s best-of-three Round One series against Nashville SC.Nashville finished top of the Eastern Conference during the regular season, 31 points ahead of ninth-placed Cincinnati. However, Cincinnati reached the series after beating Orlando in a one-off wildcard match and then claimed a 1-0 victory over Nashville in the opening game of the first-round tie.A win on Saturday would send Cincinnati into a one-off conference semi-final against either Chicago Fire or Charlotte FC. The conference final will follow before the season-ending MLS Cup final.For supporters inside TQL Stadium, the occasion will carry an additional significance. The display in The Bailey will give the club’s fans an opportunity to remember an animal whose story became closely associated with their city, regardless of the result on the pitch.
Article Summary: FC Cincinnati will honour beloved hippo Fiona with a special stadium tribute following her tragic death at the Cincinnati Zoo. The banner will be unveiled in The Bailey, the club’s main supporters’ section at TQL Stadium, ahead of the 6.30pm ET kick-off on November 28. Fiona died on November 19, aged nine, after swallowing a woollen hat that had accidentally entered her enclosure.

Article Title: Bizarre scenes in Brazil: Football manager put in chokehold by security guard after being mistaken for pitch invader during wild goal celebration
Article Text:
Paraná coach Tcheco gets caught in a security guard’s headlock after being mistaken for a pitch invader.

Security guard mistakes Paraná coach for pitch invader

Late Athletico goal takes final to penalties

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

A bizarre scene unfolded during the Copa Paraná final when Paraná Clube coach Tcheco was mistaken for a pitch invader by a security guard and grabbed in a chokehold. The 50-year-old had climbed over the perimeter fence to celebrate his side's second goal against Athletico Paranaense before attempting to return to the pitch.The incident happened on Saturday, November 21, during the second leg of the Copa Paraná final between Paraná Clube and Athletico Paranaense's reserve side at Vila Capanema in Curitiba, Brazil.Paraná had lost the first leg 1-0 at the Arena da Baixada and needed a strong home performance to overturn the deficit. They scored twice in the return fixture, taking a 2-0 lead on the night and moving 2-1 ahead on aggregate.The second goal sparked celebrations among the home supporters, with Tcheco joining them near the perimeter fence. The former midfielder, a club legend who was coaching Paraná, climbed over the barrier to celebrate with the fans before attempting to return to the field.A security guard apparently failed to recognise him and treated him as a supporter trying to enter the pitch. As Tcheco made his way back, the guard grabbed him around the neck and restrained him in a headlock.Footage of the confrontation, which has circulated on X, shows the coach struggling to free himself.The guard only released him after other members of the stadium staff intervened and explained that he was the home team's manager.The celebrations were premature, however. Paraná's 2-0 advantage had put them in position to win the Copa Paraná, but Athletico Paranaense's reserve side scored late in the match to make it 2-1 on the night and restore parity at 2-2 on aggregate.The final consequently went to a penalty shootout, which developed into a lengthy contest. Both goalkeepers missed their attempts before Athletico's goalkeeper produced the decisive save, securing an 11-10 victory in the shootout and the Copa Paraná title.Paraná had come within reach of overturning their first-leg defeat, only for the late goal and shootout to deny them the trophy. Tcheco's celebration with the supporters, meanwhile, had already produced an extraordinary moment of its own, with the coach briefly ending up in a security guard's headlock after being mistaken for one of the fans.
Article Summary: Paraná Clube coach Tcheco was mistaken for a pitch invader by a security guard. The 50-year-old had climbed over the perimeter fence to celebrate his side's second goal against Athletico Paranaense. The guard grabbed him around the neck and restrained him in a headlock. The incident happened during the second leg of the Copa Paraná final.

Article Title: Manipur to get first taste of ISL as NorthEast United face SC Delhi
Article Text:

KOLKATA: For decades, it has played the supply line for the Indian national team. Yet, on multiple occasions, especially during the ongoing conflict, it has had to see its clubs play their home games away from home.However, on Tuesday, it will come full circle for the Manipur football fans as the current top-tier Indian Super League will make its debut in Imphal as NorthEast United FC will travel to their northeast neighbours for their fixture against SC Delhi at Khuman Lumpak Main Stadium.For NEUFC players like Soraisham Dinesh Singh, Tondonba Ngasepam, Danny Laishram Meitei, Saikhom Thoiba Singh and Buanthanglun Samte, it will be a cherished chance to play in the club colours in their home state, in front of their friends and family.“I’m so happy to be home. This is my hometown. Let’s see what tomorrow (Tuesday) brings. I hope we win,” Dinesh said at the pre-match press conference in Imphal on Monday.But at the back of the mind of all the Highlanders players on the field will be an eagerness to get back to winning ways after falling to FC Goa in their last match in Guwahati, a result that ended their unbeaten run in the season.However, sitting on third spot and facing a team lying just a rung below in the table and unbeaten in their last four games, head coach Juan Pedro Benali is aware of not letting the setback on Saturday affect the players in a negative way.“The Goa game is in the past. We can’t change the result, but we can change some of the things we do on the pitch,” the Spanish coach said on Monday.NEUFC conceded with the earliest goal of the season, courtesy a defensive error from Pramveer Singh and Muhammed Nemil taking advantage with a breakthrough in the 35th second.And while they dominated most of the remaining minutes, with Alaaeddine Ajaraie, Ethyan Gonzalez and Macarton Nickson coming close to an equaliser, Benali’s men failed to recover with a goal.Ajaraie and his co-attackers will be keen to change the script in Imphal. But they would be aware of the threat from Delhi’s Carlos Fortes and Juan Pena, who have both scored three goals apiece so far.With a lot at stake for both ISL teams, the Manipur fans will hopefully be in for a treat on the field in their first encounter with top-tier Indian club football.
Article Summary: NorthEast United FC will travel to their northeast neighbours for their fixture against SC Delhi at Khuman Lumpak Main Stadium. For NEUFC players like Soraisham Dinesh Singh, Tondonba Ngasepam, Danny Laishram Meitei, Saikhom Thoiba Singh and Buanthanglun Samte, it will be a cherished chance.
